sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- Grynkewich, Warsaw Security Forum, Oct 12, on-record] NATO SACEUR set out a 'theory of victory': NATO forces would BLOCK an initial attack, BLUNT it if it persisted, and BREAK the enemy's warfighting system: 'We will break the warfighting system engaged against us by hitting both advancing forces and anything and everything that supports, sustains or controls that force.' He added he does not assess a war with Russia to be imminent or inevitable. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- WSJ, Nov 3] NATO is revising its defence strategy so that, if a member is attacked, the alliance would answer with conventional strikes deep inside Russia: military bases, supply depots, arms factories, critical infrastructure and raw-material sites, from ~150 km to several thousand km behind the front, using Tomahawk, ATACMS, Storm Shadow, Taurus, long-range missiles, rockets and drones. The plan does NOT foresee transition to nuclear weapons. [VERIFIED FACT -- public record] NATO held its first Deep Strike Symposium at SHAPE, Mons, June 17, 2026 (Grynkewich hosted, wargame included); NATO leaders at the July 7-8 Ankara summit committed in their declaration to deliver deep-precision-strike capability targets; 12 allies pledged $50bn over 10 years to long-range strike systems (WSJ via SOFX). [CONTEXT -- WSJ via yacnews] US intelligence assessments concluded in August that Putin could try to test NATO; European manufacturers have announced at least 48 low-cost cruise-missile projects among 20 companies (count by Fabian Hoffmann, Norwegian Institute for Defence Studies).
sections.what_verified: WSJ (T2) is the originator of the plan detail; SHAPE/NATO (T1, Grynkewich Oct 12 speech, public record) independently confirms the doctrine itself. Ukrainska Pravda (T3) and Kyiv Post (no declared tier) relay the WSJ report -- relays, not independent corroboration of the plan detail. Plan detail rests on WSJ attributed reporting; doctrine is dual-sourced.
sections.what_disputed: Planning is not political approval: any actual deep strike needs separate political authorization from member governments (WSJ via signaleamniyati/SOFX) -- whether European leaders would order such strikes is unsettled. Most European long-range missiles remain years away (SOFX). Russia warned Sep 30 it could use nuclear weapons if NATO tried to cut off Kaliningrad (prior scans). Grynkewich himself said war with Russia is neither imminent nor inevitable.
sections.why_matters: NATO's new war plan: strike deep inside Russia -- the 150 km to thousands-of-km doctrine, the $50bn pledge, and the one gate that decides whether it ever happens (political approval).
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (WSJ Nov 3; never recorded in Nov 3-6 scans -- grep confirmed) -- NATO revises defence plans to strike deep inside Russia if a member is attacked

totw_analysis: Our read: NATO's new war plan: strike deep inside Russia -- the 150 km to thousands-of-km doctrine, the $50bn pledge, and the one gate that decides whether it ever happens (political approval). The fault line our audience is arguing over: Deterrence or provocation? Is a public deep-strike doctrine a necessary warning that stops Russia, or an escalation that makes a NATO-Russia war more likely? Social threads split exactly there, with nuclear deterrence as the hinge ('warmongering/impossible because of nukes' vs 'normal contingency planning').
